skill.name: quality-verify
skill.description: Verify a final deliverable against completeness, correctness, consistency, performance, security, and maintainability before delivery.
skill.summary: Runs a final six-dimension quality check before a deliverable is sent.
skill.author: AbeJitsu

security_audit.summary: All nine static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced examples, or benign prose in SKILL.md. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, external command execution, or system reconnaissance behavior.

static_findings.snippet: - Quality is subjective - but consistency is objective (did it follow their standards?)

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 61-74 are a Markdown fenced block that describes a scoring algorithm in prose. There is no shell command, command substitution, or executable instruction.
Lines 74-90 contain process instructions and a transition into a JavaScript example. The backticks are Markdown formatting, not Ruby or shell execution.
Lines 90-101 show a JavaScript example using standardsRepository methods. It does not invoke a shell, spawn a process, or execute user-controlled commands.
Lines 101-103 close a Markdown code fence and reference a local standards document. This is documentation text with no external command execution.
Lines 103-107 include an inline Markdown path and the start of an example output block. No command execution primitive or unsafe runtime behavior appears there.
Lines 107-133 are an example JSON output shape. The fenced block is illustrative data, not code that executes shell commands.
Lines 133-187 close the output example and describe success criteria and sample quality checks. These are Markdown examples and prose, not executable shell content.
Lines 187-191 contain a Markdown decision tree with score thresholds. The backticks are a text fence and do not indicate command execution.
Line 198 is guidance about applying user standards consistently. It contains no request to inspect system details, enumerate host data, or perform reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Final deliverables often miss requirements, consistency checks, or security review before handoff. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured quality gate.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates deliverables across six named quality dimensions.
Calculates dimension scores and an overall quality score.
Uses project quality criteria through StandardsRepository when available.
Separates issues into critical, major, and minor groups.
Recommends whether to deliver, fix minor issues, or revise.
limitations: It depends on the deliverable and requirements present in context.
It does not run tests, linters, or scanners by itself.
It cannot verify facts without reliable source material.
Scores are more precise when project standards are available.

use_cases.title: Validate Code Before Handoff
use_cases.description: Developers can check a feature for correctness, maintainability, security, and delivery readiness before sharing it.

use_cases.title: Review Documentation Quality
use_cases.description: Technical writers can find missing sections, inconsistent examples, and unclear maintenance gaps before publishing.

use_cases.title: Standardize Final QA
use_cases.description: Project leads can apply the same quality dimensions across team deliverables and compare readiness consistently.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quality-verify to review this deliverable before I send it. Score each applicable dimension and list only issues that need action.

prompt_templates.title: Review Code Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quality-verify on this code feature. Apply available project standards, identify issue severity, and tell me if it is ready.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quality-verify to assess this documentation for completeness, accuracy, consistency, clarity, and maintainability. Recommend the smallest changes needed before delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Gate a Release Package
prompt_templates.prompt: Use quality-verify as a final release gate for this deliverable set. Compare it with requirements, project standards, and expected security checks. Provide a delivery decision.

output_examples.input: Final review of a React dropdown component.
output_examples.output: Quality score: 94/100. Ready to deliver. No critical issues found. Minor note: add one empty-state test when time allows.
Quality score: 82/100. Fix missing error response examples before delivery. Everything else follows the requested format.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a release checklist for readiness.
output_examples.output: Quality score: 68/100. Major revision recommended. The checklist is missing rollback steps, owner approvals, and security review evidence.

best_practices: Provide the final deliverable, original request, and any project standards in the same context.
Ask for issue severity so critical, major, and minor problems are separated.
Use the score as a decision aid, then fix the highest severity issues first.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a replacement for tests, linters, or security scanners.
Do not score work without the original requirements or acceptance criteria.
Do not ignore critical findings because the overall score looks high.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews completeness, correctness, consistency, performance, security, and maintainability for a final deliverable.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend tests, but it does not execute test suites unless the agent is separately asked.

faq.question: Can it use project standards?
faq.answer: Yes. It instructs the agent to load project standards through StandardsRepository when those standards are available.

faq.question: What score means ready?
faq.answer: A score of 85 or higher means ready when no critical issues are found.

faq.question: Can it review non-code work?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review documentation, plans, reports, and other structured deliverables.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: Use it when Claude, Codex, or Claude Code needs a final quality gate before delivery.
